parts.text:
18 Leonardo da Vinci proposed a flying machine that would work like a screw to lift the pilot into the
air. The ‘screw’ is rotated by the pilot.
The machine and the pilot together have a total mass of 120 kg.
Which useful output power must the pilot provide to move vertically upwards at a constant speed
of 2.5 m s–1?
A
48 W
B
300 W
C
470 W
D
2900 W

hints: Notice the motion wording: vertically upwards at constant speed of $2.5 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ with total mass $120 \text{ kg}$ - constant velocity means resultant force is zero.
Connect constant speed lifting to power: useful power is $P = Fv$, where $F$ must balance the weight $W = mg$ acting downwards.
Calculate the weight first with $g = 9.81 \text{ m s}^{-2}$, then multiply that force in $\text{N}$ by $2.5 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ to get power in $\text{W}$.
walkthrough: Identify the useful data: $m = 120 \text{ kg}$, $v = 2.5 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ upwards, and motion is at constant speed so lifting force equals weight.
State the governing rules: weight $W = mg$ and mechanical power at constant velocity $P = Fv$.
Calculate the required upward force: $F = W = mg = 120 \times 9.81 = 1177.2 \text{ N}$.
Multiply force by velocity for power: $P = 1177.2 \times 2.5 = 2943 \text{ W}$.
Check units: $\text{N} \times \text{m s}^{-1} = \text{J s}^{-1} = \text{W}$, and round to two significant figures as in the options to about $2900 \text{ W}$. This is option D.

A.explanation: Divides mass by speed, $120 / 2.5 = 48$, which ignores weight and the $P = Fv$ relationship.

B.explanation: Multiplies mass by speed, $120 \times 2.5 = 300$, which omits gravitational field strength $g$ so force is not the weight.

C.explanation: Divides weight by speed, $(120 \times 9.81)/2.5$, instead of multiplying force by velocity for power.

D.explanation: Uses $P = Fv = mgv$ with $120 \times 9.81 \times 2.5$ to give about $2900 \text{ W}$.
